title: quantized-qr-tiling-and-kv-slab-scheduler-llama-edge-cases
author: Diego Alvarez
release_notes: Improves Llama MQA/GQA throughput and latency for high-concurrency workloads by introducing QR tiling heuristics and a slab-based KV-cache scheduler; no API changes.
description:
Context: Production traffic showed periodic latency spikes and stochastic throughput drops for Llama MQA models at shard sizes that exposed misaligned QR tiling and fragmentation in the KV cache slab allocator.

Motivation: reduce  tail latency and improve sustained throughput without resorting to conservative global fallbacks.

Approach:
1) Add a quantization-aware QR tiler that prefers planar-aligned tiles for int8/int4 kernels and signals kernel hints to the router;
2) Introduce a slab-based KV-cache scheduler that bins KV allocations by sequence-length bucket and eviction pressure to reduce fragmentation and avoid expensive compaction during hot paths;
3) Hook both into the runtime kernel router to allow cheap per-request kernel hinting and fast fallback to smaller tiles when memory is constrained.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc: ENG-3421 linked in PR description
- [x] Unit tests for slab allocator edge cases
- [x] Microbenchmarks (latency and throughput) added
- [x] CI: lint/build/tests passing
- [x] Perf validation on prod-like 64-GPU pool

Commits summary:
- Add quant/qr_tiler.h and implementation to compute tile layouts for MQA/GQA models with quantized kernels (commit: "quant: qr tiler for quant kernels")
- Implement slab allocator header and tests (commit: "kv: slab allocator and basic tests")
- Implement slab scheduler with per-bucket eviction heuristics and router hooks (commit: "scheduler: slab-based kv scheduling and router integration")
- Integrate kernel hinting into kernel_router.cc with unit-level fallbacks (commit: "router: accept kernel hints from tiler/scheduler")
- Docs and benchmarks (commit: "docs: llama-quirks and bench updates")

Key changes and rationale:
- QR tiling: many quantized kernels get performance regressions when tile strides are mismatched with packed layout. The tiler calculates tile widths that align with int8/4 packing and signals when a planar kernel yields better memory coalescing. This avoids a 5-10% throughput regression observed on 4-bit kernels for sequence lengths between 512-1536.
- KV slab scheduler: previous allocator used a single freelist which fragmented under mixed sequence-length traffic. The slab scheduler creates buckets for common sequence-length groups (<=256, 257-1024, 1025-4096) and pins small allocations to avoid interleaving with large KV sets. This reduced compaction-triggered pauses by ~60% in microbench.
- Router/kernel hints: adding lightweight hints rather than hard switches lets the router prefer specialized kernels but still fall back to compatible kernels when memory/latency constraints apply.

Tests and validation:
- Unit tests cover allocator edge cases (allocation rounding, eviction under pressure, cross-bucket promotion) and tiler decision boundaries.
- Microbenchmarks: 95th percentile latency improved 9-14% across Llama MQA test matrix; sustained tokens/sec improved 12-20% depending on model size and quant level.

Bench environment: 8x A100, mixed 4-bit/8-bit quant kernels, synthetic traffic mixing short (32-64) and long (2k-4k) sequences.

CI: initial CI had intermittent flake in bench harness; fixed by stabilizing timing in tests. Final CI: all checks passed.

Review thread summary:

- Ethan: asked for fallback cost accounting in router; added telemetry counters exposed to Console (kernel_hints.{applied,fallbacks}).

Backwards compatibility and rollout:
- No public API changes.
- Feature gated at runtime via feature flag `enable_qr_slab_scheduler` (off in main by default); rollout plan: Canary -> Tiered -> Global with telemetry checks.
- Add to automated perf regression suite to detect regressions on MQA/GQA shapes.
